objective: Decide the next strategy after non-flattened NVDLA CMAC_CORE_mac Syms-image execution narrowed to timed scheduler/context semantics rather than coverage-output equivalence.

input_evidence.flattened_compute_result: five shapes pass coverage-output equivalence; many-state shapes are faster, single-state repeated-step 1x64 is slower

strategy_options.description: Represent enough of VlDelayScheduler, context time, and event queues in the uploaded state image so non-flattened timed Verilator eval can run with CPU-equivalent scheduler semantics.
strategy_options.risk: Requires lowering host containers, event queues, and context pointers into GPU-compatible state; likely delays the NN benchmark objective.

strategy_options.description: Make CPU reference mimic the current diagnostic GPU stubs and sanitized scheduler state.
strategy_options.risk: Would validate a diagnostic replay contract rather than real timed Verilator semantics; a simple CPU-side sanitization probe did not reduce coverage-output mismatches.

strategy_options.description: Keep the non-flattened timed Syms path as a non-claim and define the next NN RTL benchmark around an untimed or explicitly state-parallel workload where scheduler/context semantics are not the primary obstacle.
strategy_options.risk: Does not solve broad non-flattened hierarchy support; must preserve that non-claim explicitly.

selected_strategy.reason: The active objective is CPU-vs-hybrid NN RTL speed and testbench-shape classification. The existing evidence already shows flattened CMAC speed shape behavior, while non-flattened timed Syms remains blocked by Verilator scheduler/context semantics after targeted alignment attempts. Scheduler lowering is a larger runtime project and should not be treated as prerequisite for the next NN benchmark gate.

claim_scope: strategy selection only after non-flattened timed Syms scheduler blocker
